findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Upon arrival, there wasn't a certified food protection manager available. A CFPM arrived shortly after the start of the inspection to correct the violation. Person-in-charge (PIC) mentioned that the facility will work to get the main cook food manager certified. Ensure that there is always at least one employee who is food manager certified during operating hours.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were a handful of mouse dropping observed on floor of the dry storage area. Shown to the PIC and discussed routinely cleaning of storage area. Ensure that the area is cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent the accumulation of droppings.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: There were two containers of bread loafs stored on the floor of the indoor building. The PIC mentioned that the breads are normally stored off the floor and in a different area. Ensure that bread loafs are stored at least six inches from the floor to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer solution present inside of the shed where food is being cold held, hot held, prepped, and served. Discussed with the PIC that a sanitizer solution shall be present to sanitize all food contact surfaces. The facility will use a sanitizer bottle for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
None of the employees working at the time of the inspection could show proof of food handler certificates. The PIC was given a reference sheet of websites so that employees can obtain food handler licenses. Ensure that all employees who aren't food manager certified obtain food handler certificates. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer solution available while food prep was occurring. Discussed with PIC and a sanitizer bucket was created. Demonstrated how to properly test sanitizer solutions using (CL)test strips. Ensure that there is ALWAYS a sanitizer bucket available during hours of operation (including the shack where food is being cooked and held).
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There wasn’t a CFPM at the start of the inspection. A CFPM arrived later at the facility. Ensure that a CFPM is always present at all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
3-602.11: The facility has a number of items prepackaged in advance of sale that need proper labeling. 
1) the breading should have the labeling ON THE PACKAGE along with the name of the food and name and place of the business (see Law below). These items are pre-packaged in-advance of sale and may go home to someone’s pantry. 
2) the cakes and desserts packed for to-go meals should have the ingredients available. Create a binder with all these ingredient labels available so if a consumer needs information for allergen/sensitivity it is present.

Provide labeling. 

(A) FOOD PACKAGED in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be properly labeled. (B) Regulatory requirements-(1) The common name of the FOOD/identity statement; 106 (2) List ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, declaration of artificial colors and flavors and chemical preservatives; (3) net contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (5) MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS. Pf (6) Nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling UNLESS EXEMPT Under FDCA. (Pf) (C)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
There is a hole in floor at the entrance of the frying shack. PIC is aware of the hole and noted that it should be getting repaired soon. Ensure that that flooring is maintained and free of holes. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) The floor of the dry storage area (bathroom side area) is soiled with accumulated refuse and debris. Clean the floor. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 1. Employee in processing area did not wash hands between tasks. Employee was portioning ranch dressing and also answering the phone to take orders. Gloves were changed without a handwash occurring. Proper handwashing between glove changes and after engaging in activities that my contaminate the hands were discussed. Employee was done with food handling for the day.
2. Employee exited and re-entered the fry shack with a gloved hand. Glove was discarded, but hands were not washed prior to putting on a new glove to continue with food handling. Handwashing was discussed, and employee washed their hands prior to putting on a new glove before returning to food handling. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed upon entering the food prep and service areas, before putting on gloves and between glove changes, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not available at the handwashing sink adjacent to the 3 part sink in the main building. Paper towel holder was removed from the wall when owner painted in that area. Paper towels were provided
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted in the fry shack or at the handwashing sink adjacent to the 3 part sink in the main building. Handwashing signs were posted during inspection, and additional signs were provided for future use. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Raw shell eggs were stored above milk in the retail cooler. Foods were rearranged to allow for proper storage with eggs below and separated from ready to eat foods. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 Lid to a roaster in the fry shack fell on the ground. Employee took the lid inside to clean it. The lid was cleaned with dish soap but did not go through complete ware washing process. Proper ware washing was discussed. Ensure all food contact surfaces are washed, rinsed, and sanitized between uses or as needed when contamination may have occurred.  
Utensils and food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-501.14 Grimy, stuck on buildup was observed in the corners of the 3 part sink in the main building. Sinks were detail cleaned during inspection. Ensure basins at the three part sink are thoroughly cleaned and sanitized between uses and prior to ware washing. 
A warewashing machine; the compartments of sinks, basins, or other receptacles used for washing and rinsing equipment and utensils shall be cleaned: (A) before use, (B) throughout the day at a frequency necessary to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils and to ensure that the equipment performs its intended function; and (C) if used, at least every 24 hours.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solutions were not available for use in the processing area or in the fry shack. Food contact surface wipes that tested with quat strips (200ppm) were available. However, sanitizer solutions need to be prepared and maintained. Bleach and Quat sanitizer are both available, and test strips are available for both products. Maintain sanitizer solutions during hours of operation.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Facility is not in compliance with food handler law. Two employees working at the time had expired certifications.  Ensure all staff that are not certified food managers complete an online food handler certification course before the next routine inspection. New hires need to complete certification within 30 days of hiring. Ensure re-certification prior to expiration dates, and and maintain copies of certifications on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.
